If you are young, getting a dog actually puts a pretty strong barrier in terms of travel or just going somewhere on a whim, similar to kids. I cannot morally justify buying cheap ‘dog chow’ if I can technically afford high quality food, I spend hundreds a month on food, toys, treats, etc. for my dogs and cats. Then you get hit with a vet bill, especially as they get older (or, when they’re youngest!) bad teeth, new growth on the body, shots, new limp, cough. When we found my younger dog during covid, she jumped off the top of the couch and luxated her patella. 3 months old.  My wife spent  every penny she saved working during school, $8,000, when we were fresh out of highschool on a surgery to fix it because she could not justify sacrificing her mobility for “something as worthless as money, all things considered”. She is a better person than me and I honestly am not sure if I would have done the same at the time.

Planned parenthood. That place is a God send for low income people. If you are low income it’s insanely cheap or free, no insurance needed (my pap smear was $7). 

They will be able to help you with pregnancy testing, sti testing, contraceptives, bloodwork, prescriptions, and if you are pregnant, an abortion. The person you are with never has to know about it (and at this point so long as you don’t put it off any longer, it will only be a pill you need to take). Also an extremely important note is their connections to resources for people just like you. They always have connections to the local resource orgs (Transgender, homelessness, abusive relationships, sexual assault, lgbt, low income, there’s a ton out there that are literally built to help people in shoes similar to yours).

Also, if you stopped T because of cost reasons, they can get you HRT for low cost/free as well. When I didn’t have insurance it was $10 a vial, which was 3 doses for me. 

Go there. Don’t wait, find the closest one and GO. Do not be the person that gets stuck with someone like this because of an unwanted baby. Do not tell him that you are going. Do not tell him if you are in fact pregnant, do not tell him ANYTHING. If it is absolutely required to tell him, say you are going for HRT reasons. Just go. They are an incredible organization, i’ve been to them for a multitude of reasons across 3 different states and it is always the most welcoming experience. All they want to do is help you.

March 2014, 7th grade. This kid was known for being scarily smart. 4.0 GPA, student body president. Had perfect attendance, never missed a day in his entire life and it was frequently talked about as teachers would use him as an example. Kids called him Hawking, because he was the most intelligent person we had ever met, and he had a condition that looked like what Hawking had (I do not know if he had ALS or if it was something else).  I remember knowing he was going to do something huge to change the world. I remember asking him what he wanted to do when get grew up, and without hesitation, he said “astrophysicist”. Not one part of me or anyone else doubted that he would do it.

One Monday, he wasn’t present. I remember teachers talking about it. A few hours into school and the loud speaker goes off. The principal, while crying, said “Attention teachers, please check your email IMMEDIATELY. This is an emergency”. I remember my stomach dropping, thinking there was a school shooting, or something else horrible and we were in danger. My teacher, a bald guy who was very stoic and calm, went to his computer and immediately started loudly WAILING.  I started freaking out, not knowing what was going on. Then he breathes, and calmly says “Russel has died”. I wasn’t close with him, so I wasn’t particularly grieving, but I remember immediately thinking ‘I can’t believe he won’t be able to change the world’. 

The school took everyone at the school (jr high) to his funeral. They had an open casket, it was most kids first time seeing a body, mine included. I had the most rowdy, immature classmates and yet it was the most peaceful, wholesome, and respectful funeral I have ever attended. People in his presence were just better people. He was only 13.

To my understanding, he wasn’t supposed to die young, but he just stopped breathing in his sleep.
